summary: Decoded all 13 per-class skill pre-grant routines from `skill_pool_roll_and_class_adjust` (wpcmk file 0x4222). After rolling skill BUDGET = rng(9) + 10 (10..18), the engine dispatches via a 14-entry word jump table at file 0x4545 (CS:0x8aa9) to a per-class routine that pre-grants 1..2 skill values, deducting each from the budget. Fighter (class 0) gets nothing. Every other class gets at least one grant. All formulas fit the template: value = rng(rngRange) + sum(attrs)/divisor + constAdd; skills[slot] = value; budget -= value.

dispatch.postDispatchTail: file 0x456e..0x4585 — deducts the final grant from budget, clamping at 0
dispatch.skillArrayBase: DGROUP 0x55a4 (byte array, 30 entries, indexed by slot 0..29)

perClassRoutines.name: Lord
perClassRoutines.note: Lord and Samurai SHARE this exact routine via two jump-table entries pointing at the same file offset.

findings.claim: 13 of 14 classes get pre-granted skill values at character creation; Fighter is the only class with no grants
findings.evidence: Raw disassembly of wpcmk file 0x4222..0x4588; jump table at 0x4545 with 14 word entries; per-class routine at each entry's file offset

findings.claim: Lord (class 10) and Samurai (class 11) share the same routine (file 0x444f) via duplicated jump-table entries
findings.evidence: Jump table words 10 + 11 both point to CS:0x89b3 = file 0x444f

findings.claim: Samurai SWORD = rng(4) + (DEX+SPD)/6 + 3; for NATHAN (DEX=12, SPD=14) the range is 7..10, engine save 1 observed = 9
findings.evidence: Engine save 1 memory at DGROUP+0x55a5 = 9; formula match

findings.claim: Fighter (class 0) grants nothing; jump-table entry routes to the post-dispatch tail with [bp-c]=0
findings.evidence: Engine save 2 (NATHAN Rawulf Fighter) memory at DGROUP+0x55a4..0x55c2 = all zeros

findings.claim: Each grant deducts from the skill BUDGET pool (initial roll = rng(9) + 10); the final grant is deducted by the post-dispatch tail at 0x456e, intermediate grants deduct inline. Budget clamped at 0.
findings.evidence: Multi-grant routines (Ranger 0x42e6, Bishop 0x43ce, Monk 0x447e, Ninja 0x44e2) carry inline `sub [0x5618], [bp-c]` between grants; tail at 0x4576 does the same with cmp+clamp.

findings.claim: Grants with `(A+B)/n` always implement n as `idiv 2` followed by `idiv (n/2)` — so divisor 6 = idiv 2 then idiv 3, divisor 10 = idiv 2 then idiv 5. For positive sums (always true at creation) this equals Math.floor(sum/n).
findings.evidence: Pattern visible at every multi-attr grant (Thief 0x42c6/0x42cc; Bard 0x4359/0x435f; etc.)
